papers.title: The creatine transporter SLC6A8 is an immune pressure-exposed metabolic vulnerability in acute myeloid leukemia
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy imposes metabolic pressure that generates persisting tumor cell states, but whether these adaptations also shape immune evasion is poorly understood. Here, we identify creatine accumulation as a conserved feature of chemotherapy-persisting acute myeloid leukemia (AML) across mouse and human models. Stable-isotope tracing and genetic perturbation show that this is driven predominantly by SLC6A8-mediated creatine uptake rather than de novo synthesis. SLC6A8 was dispensable for AML proliferation and chemotherapy resistance but strongly promoted leukemia persistence under T cell pressure. This effect was independent of phosphocreatine generation and canonical energetic buffering. Instead, SLC6A8 deficiency increased cytokine-driven STAT1 signaling and chromatin remodeling, inducing the expression of antigen-presentation and co-stimulatory molecules, such as MHC-II, CD40, and CD80. Thus, creatine uptake via SLC6A8 is a non-canonical metabolic adaptation that restrains immune-driven remodeling and enables AML immune evasion. These findings link a therapy-induced metabolic adaptation to cytokine responsiveness and reveal SLC6A8 as a targetable vulnerability.

papers.title: The genetic basis of adaptation to continuous environmental gradients informs predictions about climate change responses
papers.abstract: A central goal of evolutionary genetics is to determine how environmental pressures maintain adaptive genetic variation, and evaluate how this variation is encoded in the genome. We leveraged two powerful approaches to identify genomic regions associated with climatic adaptation, test the genetic basis of climatic adaptation, and predict genomic responses to novel climates: genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of climate niche parameters derived from demographic models and genome-environment associations (GEA) of climatic factors with 2,737,409 loci. The GWAS found 319 unique single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with climate niche parameters derived from demographic models using multi-year manipulative field experiments with Boechera stricta. The GEA detected 154 unique SNPs linked to climatic variation, with only one SNP found in both approaches. Local adaptation via adult survival arose primarily through conditional neutrality, as local alleles outperformed foreign alleles at only one end of the climatic gradient, rather than genetic trade-offs. Candidate genes near these loci were implicated in stress responses. Contrary to expectations, increasing temperatures and accelerating snowmelt timings did not augment the absolute fitness of low elevation genotypes. We found non-linear fitness functions for seedling recruitment at multiple SNPs detected via GWAS, with both conditional neutrality and genetic trade-offs evident in different portions of the climatic gradient. Local maladaptation arose exclusively in GEA SNPs. Our analyses revealed that the hot and dry conditions projected under climate change may rapidly exceed the tolerance of this species. However, we identified 47 SNPs at which evolutionary rescue or assisted migration could ameliorate the reduction in fitness under climate change.

papers.title: Comprehensive identification of bacterial and archaeal habitat associations using IndicPiper
papers.abstract: Taxa that are prevalent and abundant in a particular habitat more so than other habitats can be considered indicators of that habitat. In addition to providing basic natural history information, indicator taxa can be used to verify metadata assignments in large public databases, identify potential contamination, and assess contributions of different source populations to a sink population. Despite these potential applications, a comprehensive database of microbial indicator taxa for major habitats of interest does not yet exist. Here we present IndicPiper, a database and methodology that uses the Sandpiper database combined with indicator taxa analysis to identify the habitat associations of bacterial and archaeal genera. IndicPiper includes a clearly defined methodology and set of functions such that any user with a list of habitats of interest could run the functions and generate their own database. IndicPiper uses the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) for taxonomy, and the provided database or custom databases can be used to analyze any prokaryotic sample-by-taxa abundance table, including those from shotgun metagenomic and 16S rRNA marker gene sequencing. After presenting the methodology and results, we then present three applications of IndicPiper on actual modern and ancient DNA sequencing datasets. We used IndicPiper to assess the contribution of different source habitats to Lake Tjornin sediments in Iceland over the past 2000 years, to paired indoor and outdoor dust samples from homes across the U.S, and to freshwater samples across the Willamette River watershed in Oregon, USA.

papers.title: A trade-off between desiccation resistance and social communication in a social bee
papers.abstract: The cuticular lipids of insects serve both as a barrier against desiccation and as chemical signals. In social insects, these lipids regulate reproduction and nestmate recognition, potentially creating a trade-off between waterproofing and communication. We tested this hypothesis in bumblebee workers by examining the roles of cuticular compounds in desiccation resistance and behavioral attraction. Desiccation survival varied with age, social state, and ovary activation, with fertile queenless workers showing the greatest resistance. Cuticular profiles changed markedly with age and social environment. Although the total amount of secretion remained similar among groups, queenright workers showed age-dependent decline in alkenes and a corresponding increase in two acetate esters (tetracosyl and hexacosyl acetate). To determine the functions of these compounds, we tested their effects on desiccation survival and attraction. Topical application of several hydrocarbons, but not tetracosyl acetate, increased desiccation resistance. In contrast, tetracosyl acetate, but not hydrocarbons, elicited attraction, and only in queenright workers. These results demonstrate an age-dependent shift in cuticular lipid composition in the presence of the queen from producing waterproofing hydrocarbons toward signaling compounds in the presence of the queen, reducing desiccation resistance while enhancing communication. Our findings suggest that the evolution of insect cuticular lipids has been shaped by both physiological demands and selection for complex social communication.

papers.title: Beyond the tripartite genome: a widespread, mobile and gene-rich accessory plasmidome expands the genomic landscape of the model symbiont Sinorhizobium meliloti
papers.abstract: Sinorhizobium meliloti is one of the best-studied nitrogen-fixing symbionts, yet research has focused almost entirely on its chromosome and two megaplasmids, pSymA and pSymB. Many strains carry additional accessory plasmids, but these large, pSymA-like elements are rarely recovered from short-read assemblies, leaving a hidden part of the genome unexplored. By sequencing 346 strains with long reads, we recovered 386 accessory plasmids from 76% of strains, with 318 absent from public databases, showing that accessory plasmids are the rule and not the exception. These plasmids were large (34-749 kb), including the largest accessory plasmid reported in S. meliloti, and most were mobilizable or conjugative (relaxases in 85% and mating-pair formation systems in 75% of plasmid clusters), equipping them to move between strains. RepA typing defined 13 replicon groups unique to Sinorhizobium, which could serve as a framework for tracking these plasmids in natural populations. We also found evidence of plasmid expansion by fusion, and one ~315 kb plasmid was a cointegrate of two smaller plasmids from our collection. About two-thirds of plasmid gene families were absent from the main replicons, including defense systems, the anti-restriction protein ArdC, and biosynthetic gene clusters, 53% of which had never been observed before. Overturning the view that S. meliloti lacks restriction-modification systems, we found them in 153 genomes, including on 32 accessory plasmids. Most inferred gene transfers stayed within the family Rhizobiaceae. Accessory plasmids thus form a large, mobile and largely unexplored gene pool that may shape how this model symbiont competes and adapts.

papers.title: Gene identity, not recoding strategy, determines the fitness cost of synonymous recoding in bacteriophage {Phi}X174
papers.abstract: Synthetic biology allows for the synthesis of genomes from scratch. Although technically achievable, our abilities in designing genomes that result in live organisms are in their infancy. One important consideration is synonymous codon usage bias, which is present in most organisms and shaped by selection for efficient translation. Many studies have edited the synonymous codon usage patterns of viruses with the goal of viral attenuation, but these studies almost always build a single construct per design, so we know little about how repeatable the effects of recoding are. We designed and built 111 synonymously recoded {Phi}X174 genomes, applying four recoding strategies at up to five levels of attenuation to each of three genes, with three independently designed replicates of most combinations. Which gene we recoded mattered considerably more than how we recoded it. Recoding genes for the major capsid protein F, the major spike protein G and the DNA pilot protein H in full, with the least-used synonym codons from E. coli cost 12.0, 10.8 and 5.9 doublings per hour, respectively. Recoding strategy per se had no detectable effect once the number of codons changed was accounted for. Predicted mRNA folding stability also had no measurable effect on fitness when tested in gene F, whose wildtype transcript is highly stable and could easily be destabilized with synonymous codon rearrangements. While the number of codons changed was correlated with the degree of attenuation, divergence between independently designed replicates increased as more codons were edited. Replicates of designs with small fitness effects varied little, while replicates of strongly attenuating designs diverged by several doublings per hour. The fitness outcome of large-scale genome recoding is therefore substantially unpredictable from the design variables alone: even among independently designed genomes receiving the same treatment, fitness can diverge substantially.

papers.title: Pharmacological CARD9 Inhibition Reduces Pneumocystis murina Burden In Vivo and Ex Vivo
papers.abstract: Caspase recruitment domain-containing protein 9 (CARD9) is an important adaptor protein of the innate immune responses to various fungal pathogens, including Pneumocystis species. CARD9 signaling is paramount in Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) host defense, and excessive inflammatory responses driven by this molecule can promote deleterious lung injury. We previously demonstrated that BRD5529, a first generation small-molecule CARD9 inhibitor, attenuates pulmonary inflammatory cytokine production during PCP. Here, we investigated the previously unreported effects of BRD5529 on Pneumocystis murina burden in vivo and in an ex vivo PCP-infected precision-cut lung slice (PCLS) model. In vitro, BRD5529 treatment (1 mg/kg) reduced lung organism burden in mice with established PCP, with an effect similar in magnitude to standard-of-care trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) therapy. In infected PCLS cultured with BRD5529 for 72 h, P. murina viability was also reduced, with the greatest reduction observed at lower BRD5529 concentrations. BRD5529 treatment did not reduce PCLS metabolic activity and viability after 72 h, as assessed by resazurin reduction. Together, these findings suggest that pharmacological CARD9 inhibition may impact organism burden/viability in addition to reducing lung inflammation during PCP.

papers.title: Linking Early Bacterial Responses to Growth Inhibition via Glucose-Turbidity Dynamics for Rapid Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing
papers.abstract: Earlier susceptibility information can guide timely antibiotic selection, while metabolic measurements can broaden the characterization of bacterial drug responses. We developed glucose-turbidity antimicrobial susceptibility testing (GT-AST) to pair residual-glucose assay signals with turbidity and relate early responses to growth inhibition. Among 43 cultured isolates, some antibiotic-exposed cultures showed glucose-associated changes despite attenuated turbidity responses. These observations provide physiological clues for studying metabolic activity when growth is limited, including future investigations of viable but non-culturable states or persister cells. Conventional broth microdilution relies on overnight growth readings; GT-AST used trajectories collected during approximately 2 h of antibiotic exposure to predict subsequent growth and estimate minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). Across 100 repeats of isolate-grouped cross-validation, essential agreement between predicted MICs and independently measured reference MICs averaged 87.1%. Eight bronchoalveolar lavage fluid specimens were tested directly without prior bacterial isolation. Levofloxacin susceptibility classifications based on observed growth agreed with hospital results in all four culture-positive specimens. Exact and essential agreement between predicted and hospital MICs each averaged 99.0%. Together, these findings support developing GT-AST to provide earlier susceptibility information for effective, appropriately targeted treatment of patients. Keywords: antimicrobial susceptibility testing; glucose metabolism; turbidity; machine learning; minimum inhibitory concentration

papers.title: Candidate gene mining of a fragmented Tipularia discolor Pursh (Nutt.) genome assembly reveals genes putatively associated with specialized metabolite production.
papers.abstract: Orchids are a large and diverse group of plants with unique adaptations that have enabled the utilization of many different environmental habitats across almost all continents. These adaptations are mediated by an as-yet-underexplored genetic resource. Nearly all sequenced orchid genomes are of Asian origin and represent less than 0.1% of all orchid species, limiting the ability to explore and mine the gene space of this complex plant family. Greater representation of orchids in genome databases could provide important insights into the genes responsible for adaptive phenotypes, which could be useful for targeted crop improvement and in orchid conservation efforts. To begin to expand the palette of orchid genomes, an effort was undertaken to sequence the genome of a North American terrestrial orchid, Tipularia discolor. K-mer analysis estimated a haploid genome size of approximately 1.7 Gb, with a high proportion of repetitive sequences. Although a complete genome was not obtained, the implementation of a conservative gene mining approach and the generation of a candidate gene mining pipeline led to the identification of 68 consensus contig objects containing whole or partial genes related to sucrose, trehalose, terpenoid, and phenylpropanoid metabolism. Of note, two bibenzyl synthase homologs were identified with high confidence and clustered with characterized orchid bibenzyl synthases in a CHS/BBS phylogeny, indicating that T. discolor, like its Asian and South American relatives, has the capacity to produce this distinct class of phenylpropanoids. Thus, despite substantial fragmentation, the T. discolor assembly contains sufficient gene space representation for targeted candidate gene discovery. This works lays the foundation for functional characterization of selected candidates and development of a more complete genome assembly for comparative genomic studies.

papers.title: Resistance-Breaking Root-knot Nematode Isolates Across California Tomato Fields Show Virulence Differences on Rotation Crops and Genomic Polymorphisms
papers.abstract: Root-knot nematodes (RKNs) are a major concern for tomato growers worldwide. Management relies heavily on the plant resistance gene Mi-1, which has been bred into most processing tomato cultivars. However, repeated use of Mi-1 has placed strong selection pressure on nematode populations, promoting the emergence of resistance-breaking isolates. Despite the growing impact of resistance-breaking RKNs, their frequency, distribution, and species identity across California remain poorly understood. In this study, we isolated RKN isolates from processing tomato fields at 14 sites across California, identified them to species, and evaluated their reproduction on current rotation crops to determine whether crop rotation could suppress these populations. All 14 sites yielded resistance-breaking populations, and most isolates were M. incognita. A SNP-based principal component analysis revealed substantial genetic diversity among several isolates, suggesting that resistance-breaking emerged independently in multiple fields rather than all spreading from a single population. In greenhouse assays, alfalfa displayed the lowest reproduction of both wild-type and resistance-breaking M. incognita, whereas reproduction on other rotation crops varied by isolate. Together, these results show that rotation decisions should be guided by local RKN population identity and host compatibility rather than generalized strategies across fields.

papers.title: Meta(xylem)morphoses: Root vascular patterning is dynamic and convergent in temperate grasses
papers.abstract: In cereal roots the metaxylem vessels are the main channels of axial water transport. Metaxylem size and number are considered constant traits characterising different root classes. Here we show that metaxylem number is progressively remodelled along root axes, producing mature roots with vascular anatomy differing by position. At initiation, adventitious wheat root tips produce multiple files of metaxylem, and then progressively fewer, until a single central metaxylem file exists, resembling the vascular anatomy of the seminal roots. This pattern was observed in wheat, barley, rye, oat, and Brachypodium, but not in maize or sorghum. We investigated the developmental regulation of this phenomenon by creating a cell-resolved spatial transcriptomic atlas of wheat adventitious root tips in these different metaxylem production states and integrated this with bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole root tips. We developed a pipeline integrating these complementary transcriptomic datasets to reveal differentially expressed genes that included candidates controlling meristem maintenance, vascular patterning, and metaxylem wall lignification. Hydraulic modelling revealed changes in vessel number reduces pressure in vasculature, while maintaining or increasing the capacity of roots to transport water. We propose that this developmental transition preconfigures different regions of the root for their changing hydraulic environments, providing a mechanism to balance hydraulic robustness and efficiency over the root life cycle.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of lncRNAs in Wheat Leaf Rust Pathogen Interactions
papers.abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is a major crop grown on about 225 million hectares worldwide, and it suffers heavy losses from rusts caused by fungal pathogens. This study focuses on leaf rust, caused by Puccinia triticina. When wheat is attacked by this fungus, hundreds of downstream genes in various biological pathways show regulated expression, which depends partly on non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs) and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). Because lncRNAs are both regulators and sources of miRNAs, understanding lncRNA-miRNA relationships is important for understanding gene regulation. RNA-seq data from the EMBL-EBI archive were quality-checked with FastQC, aligned with HISAT2 and assembled with StringTie. Transcripts shorter than 200 nucleotides (nt) and other ncRNAs (rRNA, tRNA and snoRNA) were removed, and coding potential was assessed with CPC2 and PLEK, followed by BLASTX against Pfam to remove protein-coding sequences. Differential expression was analysed with NOISeq, and lncRNA-miRNA interactions were predicted with psRNATarget. In total, 7,390 presumed lncRNAs were identified, of which 5,496 were differentially expressed in susceptible and resistant wheat lines. LncRNA targets of 59 miRNAs were analysed; these miRNAs have been reported to regulate plant disease-related genes such as the SPL and NAC families and the cyclophilins TaCYP61, TaCYP62, TaCYP43, TaCYP76 and TaCYP81.

papers.title: Ultrasonic emissions of sunflower and buckwheat carry species identity in their spectrum and drought in their rate
papers.abstract: Plants under water deficit produce ultrasonic acoustic emissions that can be recorded in air. Species have been compared mainly by peak frequency. We report, to our knowledge, the first airborne recordings of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) and buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum), with gas exchange and chlorophyll fluorescence on the same plants. Across 119 recordings of 30 min each, made on two drought and two watered end plants per species, every drought plant emitted more events over the series than the watered plants. Rates rose 107 fold in sunflower and 5.3 fold in buckwheat, coincided with low stomatal conductance, and later fell in single plants. In sunflower, emission was already raised when maximum Photosystem II quantum yield was similar between treatments. At equal loudness, sunflower events carried a median of 24% of their energy at 40-80 kHz, against 2% in buckwheat, in drought and watered plants alike, although both species peaked near 30 kHz. In a proof of concept on four plants per species, this share identified a held-out plant's species in 96% of draws of five events. Airborne ultrasound thus carries species identity in its spectrum and drought in its event rate, two signals a non-contact sensor could combine.

papers.title: Cell-Cycle Regulation In Planta: Linking Nucleus Geometry and CYCB1;1 Marker Accumulation.
papers.abstract: Cell division is a fundamental biological process underlying plant growth and devel-opment and ensuring the transmission of genetic and epigenetic information. Although cell-cycle regulation has been extensively investigated using suspension-cultured cells and molecular reporters, these experimental systems do not fully reproduce the hor-monal environment, cellular identity, and chromatin organization of cells within intact plant tissues. From a physical perspective, cell-cycle progression also involves sub-stantial structural remodeling of genetic material, particularly during the transition from the G2 nuclear configuration to condensed mitotic chromosomes. The magnitude of this remodeling may depend on the initial geometry and organization of chromatin. Here, we quantitatively characterized nuclear and chromatin architecture in different cell types of the Arabidopsis thaliana root, focusing on the structural differences be-tween G2 and mitotic states. In parallel, we assessed CYCB1 reporter expression using GUS and GFP signal intensities. We found that epidermal and cortical cells exhibited greater G2-to-M structural distances accompanied by higher CYCB1 reporter signals, whereas inner root tissues showed smaller structural distances and lower reporter in-tensities. These findings reveal a relationship between cell-type-specific chromatin architecture and CYCB1 reporter accumulation. We propose that differences in the structural re-modeling required for mitotic entry contribute to the spatial heterogeneity of cell-cycle regulation in plant tissues. Importantly, CYCB1 reporter intensity should not be interpreted as a direct or universal quantitative measure of cell-cycle activity across structurally distinct cell types. Instead, quantitative analysis of nuclear geometry and chromatin organization provides an important complementary approach for investigat-ing the physical requirements of cell-cycle transitions in intact plant tissues.

papers.title: Biologically Guided Deep Learning for Personalized PSA Forecasting in Intermittent Prostate Cancer Therapy
papers.abstract: Intermittent Androgen Deprivation Therapy (IADT) offers a promising management strategy for prostate cancer by alternating treatment periods with the aim of delaying castration resistance and mitigating side effects. An evolutionary rationale for treatment interruptions is to preserve treatment-sensitive cells that may competitively suppress resistant populations. However, designing optimal patient-specific treatment schedules remains challenging due to the complex dynamics of tumor evolution and the computational intensity of traditional mechanistic simulation models. Standard mathematical models have prespecified structures that may inadequately capture patient-specific tumor evolution, limiting Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) forecasting accuracy and adaptation to new patient data. These limitations may reduce the effectiveness of treatment policies learned using these models. To address them, we present a domain-adapted machine learning framework that integrates biological constraints into the deep learning architecture and embeds historical biomarkers to act as a robust, computationally efficient neural surrogate for mechanistic simulations. This framework enhances generalization across sparse clinical profiles by leveraging deep neural representations for patient-specific and cross-patient parameter learning, and potentially enables the identification of personalized dosing schedules tailored to individual tumor trajectories. Preliminary evaluations confirm that it reliably captures treatment-associated PSA dynamics while overcoming the computational bottlenecks of numerical solvers. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable foundation for optimizing adaptive therapy protocols to extend time to disease progression. We present the architectural formulation, forecasting evaluation against mechanistic baselines, and training and optimization procedures of the deep neural networks.

papers.title: Spatial single cell multi-omics identifies divergent melanoma-cell states associated with metastatic outcomes in thin primary melanomas
papers.abstract: Thin melanomas (Breslow thickness [≤]1 mm) generally have favorable outcomes, yet some metastasise, highlighting the need for biomarkers of progression. Here, we combined same-section single-cell spatial transcriptomics and proteomics to identify seven melanoma-cell states organized along two inferred trajectories sharing a common trunk, extending from an in situ epithelial-adjacent state through developmental stress to melanocytic differentiation before diverging into two lineages. Lineage 1 progressed through an IFN-associated stress intermediate state towards mesenchymal-invasive cells enriched in metastasizing tumors and associated with immune-hot neighborhoods, extracellular-matrix remodeling and angiogenesis, potentially supporting vascular mimicry and metastatic dissemination. Lineage 2 terminated in cohesive nevus-like cells retaining melanocytic features within relatively immune-cold neighborhoods and enriched in non-metastasizing tumors. We confirmed these associations using H&E-inferred spatial transcriptomics in an international multicentric cohort and independent bulk transcriptomic datasets in primary melanomas, linking spatially organized melanoma-cell programs to metastatic outcome and identifying potential biomarkers of progression in thin melanoma.

papers.title: All the diversity we cannot see: Using single-cell population genetics to reveal the reproductive mode of the snow alga Chlainomonas sp. (Chlorophyta)
papers.abstract: Many organisms responsible for globally important processes, from carbon cycling to human disease, are microscopic eukaryotes. While their reproduction is essential for their success, across the tree of life, our understanding of evolutionary processes is limited due to the inherent challenges of studying microorganisms. Tools and predictions developed in multicellular and obligately sexual taxa are often not tractable in microbes, where population sizes can be large and extracting DNA from individuals is difficult. Even when sexual characteristics can be observed, population genetics is the only method available to characterize the reproductive mode. The relative rates of sexual versus clonal reproduction partition genetic diversity and are therefore integral to our understanding of evolutionary processes. We developed a single-cell population genetic approach to characterize the reproductive mode of the snow alga Chlainomonas sp. This Chlorophyte alga exhibits a complex life cycle, whereby bloom dynamics are directly observable in natural populations. We explored genetic diversity using single cells collected across several years of Chlainomonas sp. summer blooms. Dominant red cells in the bloom were diploid. Yet, all were unique genotypes, despite the prediction that clonal processes drive bloom development. We found high selfing rates, but selfing and clonality are often indistinguishable without understanding an organisms's natural history. Chlainomonas sp. has a haploid-diploid life cycle as hypothesized, engaging in both clonal and sexual reproduction, likely selfing. This study represents a first use of single cell population genetic methods to understand natural populations of partially clonal microeukaryotes.

papers.title: 5-Azacytidine alleviates Liver Fibrosis via modulation of TET1 and TET3 levels and restoration of global 5hmC
papers.abstract: DNA methylation and demethylation processes play a pivotal role in the onset and progression of liver diseases. The ten-eleven translocase enzymes (TET1, TET2 and TET3) are key DNA demethylases that oxidise 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), thereby regulating the cellular epigenetic state. Dysregulated TET expression has been increasingly associated with hepatic pathology. In this study, we assessed the DNA hydroxymethylation status of fibrotic and regenerating livers and correlated these changes with TET protein expression in a CCl induced murine model of liver fibrosis. Fibrosis progression was accompanied by a progressive, stage-wise reduction in hydroxymethylation, assessed by 5hmC immunostaining, together with a corresponding decrease in TET1 and increase in TET3 protein levels detected by immunoblotting. TET1 immunostaining correlated with the pattern of 5hmC immunostaining in fibrotic liver tissue. Treatment with the epigenetic agent 5-Azacytidine (5-AZA) improved liver morphology and lowered serum AST and ALT activities. 5-AZA treatment restored 5hmC levels and TET1 expression while downregulating TET3 in total liver tissue. Complementary in vitro studies in mouse primary and human stellate cells (LX-2) corroborated an increase in TET3 that correlated with elevated 5hmC, both of which were attenuated in stellate cells treated with 5-AZA. The reduction in TET3 corresponded with decreased expression of fibrogenic markers; -smooth muscle actin and Collagen-I. Collectively, this study identifies a progressive loss of 5hmC during liver fibrosis and demonstrates that pharmacological modulation via an epigenetic agent restores 5hmC homeostasis and TET-associated hydroxymethylation, attenuating fibrotic remodelling. These findings support targeting the DNA methylation-demethylation axis, and TET regulation in particular, as a promising therapeutic avenue for liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Structural and Metabolic Insufficiency of the Blood-Brain Barrier Is Associated with Schizophrenia Penetrance
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly specialized vascular endothelial network tightly regulating peripheral influences on the brain. BBB endothelial cells (ECs) are mitochondrially rich compared to peripheral ECs, and mitochondrial function has been linked with the induction of BBB properties. In the 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS), a condition with heightened risk for schizophrenia (SZ), we demonstrated rescue of BBB properties by restoring mitochondrial function. Thus, we sought to understand if energetic and structural capacities of the BBB may influence the SZ penetrance seen in 22qDS. We differentiated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from control, 22qDS individuals without SZ (22qDS(-)SZ), and 22qDS individuals with SZ (22qDS + SZ) into BBB-like cells (iBBB). We found that the iBBBs derived from 22qDS + SZ display considerable reductions in the rate of oxygen consumption as compared to 22qDS without (22qDS(-)SZ). Furthermore, 22qDS(-)SZ iBBB retain control-level barrier characteristics, including resistance to ionic flux, and enhanced tight junction and cytoskeletal properties. These phenotypes were further reinforced by RNA sequencing, which implicated several metabolic-, cytoskeletal-, and cell-cell adhesion-related differentially expressed genes, and ontological and gene-set enrichment phenotypes. Together, our functional and transcriptomic data indicate a dual compensation in metabolic and structural programs specific to the 22qDS subgroup lacking a SZ diagnosis. Thus, the penetrance of SZ in the BBB strongly associates with the capacity to maintain structural and metabolic phenotypes, representing a defining feature of 22qDS-related SZ pathophysiology. These findings bridge a gap in knowledge of molecular features which characterize differential phenotypes in the psychosis subtypes of 22qDS and address divergent BBB cell biology between individuals with and without SZ.

papers.title: Translation of small ORFs in non-canonical RNAs provides resilience to heat shock stress
papers.abstract: Background: Heat shock and other stress conditions severely challenge cell and organismal survival. Characterising and understanding the genome responses to heat shock is of increasing interest due to the accelerated impact of global warming. Under heat shock and other stress conditions, the translation of most canonical genes is reduced as part of a physiological response to improve cellular and organismal resilience. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are among a minority of proteins whose expression increases during heat shock, working as chaperones and helping other proteins to maintain their tertiary structure. Results: In contrast to canonical genes, whose translation is dramatically suppressed under heat shock conditions, we find that the translation of small Open Reading Frames (smORFs), especially those in so-called long-noncoding, (or long noncanonical) RNAs (lncRNAs), remains at similar levels, and in some cases is enhanced under heat shock in Drosophila melanogaster. lncRNA translation under heat stress entails a 3' shift in the smORFs translated in a given lncRNA, a shift that may be favoured by non-canonical smORF translation mechanisms. We also characterise two smORFs with stress-enhanced translation, showing that their expression is up-regulated by the heat stress response pathway, and that their microproteins improve organism survival and resilience under heat shock. Conclusion: smORF and lncRNA translation is more resilient to heat shock than that of standard genes, and this smORF translation can increase organismal resilience to heat shock, potentially representing a new component of the HSF stress-response gene regulation pathway. The stress-resilient lncRNA translation entails a 3' shift in the position and translation levels of smORFs being translated, and while the full molecular mechanism of this shift is not known at the moment, we propose that it might take advantage of non-canonical aspects of polycistronic lncRNA translation.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Host Gene Expression Patterns Associated with Naegleria fowleri Infection in the Murine Brain
papers.abstract: Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis (PAM), caused by the free-living amoebae Naegleria fowleri, is a devastating disease with a mortality rate exceeding 97%. Despite its severity, the spatial and temporal characteristics of the host immune response to infection within the brain remain poorly understood. Here, we used spatially resolved transcriptomic profiling to characterize region-specific gene expression patterns in brain tissue collected at multiple time points following intranasal inoculation of N. fowleri in mice. Our analysis revealed pronounced pro-inflammatory transcriptional signatures that varied across brain regions and over the course of infection. Cell type-associated gene expression profiles suggested the involvement of several immune cell populations, including macrophages, neutrophils, and natural killer T cells, alongside transcriptional changes associated with neural cell populations. Notably, inflammatory transcriptional signatures also were detected in brain regions without detectable amoebae, indicating that host responses extend beyond regions of apparent parasite localization. Collectively, these findings provide a spatial and temporal characterization of the host transcriptional response during experimental PAM, highlighting inflammatory gene expression signatures and putative immune and neural cell populations associated with disease progression. This study provides a foundation for future investigations into the cellular and molecular processes underlying neuroinflammation during N. fowleri infection.

papers.title: A differential-trend-subtype strategy for integrated serum proteomics and N-glycoproteomics reveals ovarian cancer-associated remodelling
papers.abstract: Protein glycosylation is increasingly implicated in cancer, but its macro- and microheterogeneity complicate cohort-scale resolution of disease-associated remodeling. Here we performed matched peptide-level proteomic (PEP) and intact N-glycopeptide (NGP) profiling of serum from 100 participants, comprising 23 healthy controls, 27 individuals with benign ovarian disease and 50 patients with ovarian cancer. We identified 12,634 intact NGPs with plausible linkages spanning 6,127 protein-site glycosites and 4,438 glycoproteins. We developed a Differential-Trend-Subtype (DTS) target-prioritization framework integrating ovarian cancer versus non-malignant differences, cross-sectional healthy-benign-cancer trends and within-cancer subtype effects. Independent PEP and NGP clustering supported two aligned molecular states, assigning 47 of 50 cancer samples concordantly. Among 171 subtype-associated NGPs, cluster 1-high (C1-high) features were more frequently fucosylated, whereas cluster 2-high (C2-high) features were more frequently sialylated. DTS strategy prioritized a more informative pool of candidate features. Under leakage-controlled nested resampling, the best exploratory diagnostic panel-comprising PON1, HP and C9 peptide features together with an IGHM N209 N-glycopeptide-achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.843+-0.026, whereas the best subtype panel-comprising C2 N621 and IGHG1 N180 N-glycopeptides together with SERPINA3-achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.997+-0.005. These findings demonstrate the utility of DTS for prioritizing candidate markers and reveal coordinated protein and site-specific N-glycan remodelling with potential relevance to ovarian cancer diagnosis and molecular stratification.

papers.title: CsrA-dependent RNA accessibility landscapes prioritize new mRNA and sRNA targets and link CsrA to polyphosphate homeostasis
papers.abstract: The global RNA-binding protein CsrA (Carbon Storage Regulatory Protein A) regulates diverse physiological processes in Gammaproteobacteria, but the full set of RNAs through which it actuates and how they intersect with small RNA (sRNA) regulation and stress physiology remain incompletely defined. We asked how CsrA shapes RNA accessibility across 431 untranslated mRNA regions and 87 sRNAs in Escherichia coli. Using a previously published RNA accessibility profiling method (INTERFACE), we compared wild type and CsrA mutant (csrA::kan) strains. Permissive screening for accessibility peaks at GGA/AGA motifs nominated 87 5'UTRs, 32 3'UTRs and 28 sRNAs as candidate responsive RNAs but did not pass a permutation null (p=0.43), however it can be used to guide selection of candidates for validation. Eleven 5'UTRs had no prior experimental evidence, and all 3'UTRs and most sRNAs were nominated manually because of limited probe numbers in these targets. In reporter assays, six of nine RNAs tested showed CsrA-dependent expression (mdtE, ribB, patA, metC, ppk and proS) including three candidate activated-targets, although only two of five reporters from the primary candidate list responded. CsrA bound the sRNAs SsrA and RalA in vitro, and reporter assays suggested CsrA-dependent modulation of previously identified ArrS-ribB and GcvB-crp interactions. Mutating sequence elements in the ppk 5' UTR altered CsrA-dependent expression, and loss of CsrA-activity was associated with reduced polyphosphate and fewer Hfq-containing HP-bodies during nitrogen starvation. Together, these findings expand the CsrA regulon and its overlap with sRNA networks, and support accessibility profiling to prioritize RNA-binding protein targets for follow-up characterization.

papers.title: A deep-learning predictive model for Cas12a activity in wheat
papers.abstract: CRISPR technology has created targeted DNA mutations across the tree of life. Target sites are defined by RNA molecules that largely determine the efficiency of an experiment. Several predictive models are available to select the most efficient RNAs. Unfortunately, these models are not built with plant data and have limited predictive power in plant systems. To overcome this limitation, we established a high-throughput arrayed wheat protoplast transfection method and measured the editing efficiency of ~1,000 unique LbCas12a crRNAs at on- and off-target sites. We trained different models by testing 40 deep learning architectures and found that a convolutional neural network model called 2CaP-5 displayed the best performance. While 2CaP-5 had moderate to strong predictive power in protoplasts, it did not generalize to Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Despite this limitation, we demonstrate that 2CaP-5 can be re-trained with as few as 500 crRNAs. The use of such a small training set is advantageous for low-throughput experimental systems such as typically found in transgenic plant systems. We also used ~2,000 off-targets in the wheat subgenomes to investigate Cas12a specificity. Our dataset confirms previous observations regarding off-targets, specifically that single mismatches reduce indel efficiency provided they are adjacent to the PAM and that off-target activity can be largely prevented by three mismatches. Altogether, our results show that the 2CaP-5 model has moderate to strong predictive power for Cas12a crRNAs in wheat protoplasts and will serve as a useful foundation for predictive tools in other plant species.

papers.title: Distinct spatial domains of auxin perception control root growth in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Primary root morphogenesis is coordinated by the integrated action of cell division, expansion, and differentiation. Although auxin is a central regulator of root development, how the spatial context of auxin perception shapes growth dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we implement a synthetic auxin perception system that enables tissue-specific manipulation of auxin signaling output in defined spatial domains of the Arabidopsis thaliana root. Using this approach, we show that root growth depends primarily on the integration of local auxin perception in elongating cells of the outermost root tissue layers. Computational modeling predicts that mutually exclusive auxin sensitivity domains shift the position of the cell proliferation boundary, which was validated experimentally. We further found that elongating cells exhibit greater sensitivity to auxin input than meristematic cells, and that this differential responsiveness is critical for determining the overall root length. Together, our results identify mutually exclusive spatial domains of auxin sensitivity that coordinate root morphogenesis.

papers.title: Spatial co-enrichment of immature myeloid and T-cell populations predicts survival in NPM1-mutant AML
papers.abstract: NPM1-mutant acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the most common molecularly defined AML subtype. Outcomes vary considerably across co-mutational profiles, and the bone marrow (BM) microenvironment may shape treatment responses through immune cell interactions. Whether these interactions form spatially organized structures with independent prognostic relevance in the diagnostic BM is unknown. We used CO-Detection by indEXing (CODEX) with a 54-marker panel and MERFISH spatial transcriptomics to profile 67 NPM1-mutant AML patients at diagnosis and 38 age- and sex-matched normal BM (NBM) controls on tissue microarrays from archival FFPE samples, profiling 1,494,397 cells and annotating 27 cell types. Compared to NBM, NPM1-mutant AML showed striking architectural reorganization, including a loss of stroma association with adaptive immune cells and loss of NBM-specific mature myeloid and erythroid cellular neighborhoods. AML was characterized by expansion of phenotypically distinct immature myeloid (IM) populations with aberrant immunophenotypes, including CD11b+ VISTA+ and CD15+ subsets, alongside an expansion of CD8+ and PD1+ CD4+ T-cells. While cell type and neighborhood cluster frequencies showed limited prognostic associations, spatial context-dependent interactions were more informative. Both enrichment of CD11b+ IM in adaptive immune neighborhoods, and co-enrichment with CD8+ T-cells were adversely associated with overall survival. Spatial transcriptomics identified upregulated genes associated with monocytic AML in CD11b+ IM cells and candidate immunosuppressive ligand-receptor interactions, including TGFB1-TGFBR1 and JAG1-NOTCH1, with T-cells. These findings indicate that spatial context of suppressor-immune cell interactions carries prognostic information not captured by genomics or cell type frequencies alone and is amenable to translation using routine diagnostic FFPE samples.

papers.title: Multiple isoforms of cancer stemness regulator NanogP8 in clinical prostate cancer specimens and their unique biochemical and oncogenic properties
papers.abstract: The pluripotency regulator Nanog (NANOG, for human protein) has been reported to be overexpressed in cancers and in cancer stem cells (CSCs). We have previously shown that NanogP8, encoded by one of the expressed Nanog pseudogenes, is the predominant transcript expressed in several cancers including prostate cancer (PCa). We have also demonstrated that NanogP8 is functionally important in tumorigenesis as its loss impairs tumor regeneration and growth while inducible expression of NanogP8 is sufficient to reprogram androgen-dependent PCa to an androgen-independent and castration-resistant state. In the current study, we combined RT-PCR, subcloning and sequencing to systematically analyze the open reading frame sequences of Nanog and NanogP8 mRNA transcripts in treatment-naive clinical human PCa (HPCa) specimens. Our results revealed that HPCa did not express the ES cell-specific Nanog1 mRNA but primarily expressed NanogP8 together with several other Nanog pseudogenes including NanogP7 and NanogP6. Interestingly, most HPCa specimens contained multiple isoforms of NanogP8 transcripts, and we identified novel missense mutations in the NanogP8 transcripts that could lead to amino acid changes. Experiments with recombinant proteins, site-directed mutagenesis and Western blotting revealed several mutations that conferred the NanogP8 variant proteins, including NanogP8L61P, NanogP8D64Y, and NanogP8N130S, with unique biochemical properties. Moreover, some mutations furnish NanogP8 isoforms with distinct CSC and oncogenic characteristics. Altogether, this study advances our knowledge of the molecular, biochemical and oncogenic properties of Nanog expression and NanogP8 isoforms in PCa.

papers.title: TEAD Palmitoylation Inhibitors are Brain Penetrant and Enhance Survival in Preclinical Models of Recurrent Glioblastoma in Combination with Standard-of-Care Therapy
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Oncogenic addiction to YAP-TEAD signaling drives adaptive plasticity, therapeutic resistance, invasion and tumor progression in many cancers, including in glioblastoma (GBM), and represents an actionable vulnerability to explore as adjuvant therapy during tumor recurrence. This study evaluated the translational potential of orally bioavailable Vivace Therapeutics (VT) TEAD palmitoylation inhibitors in preclinical GBM models. Experimental Design: The effects of VT103 and VT104 on GBM proliferation, migration, and TEAD activity were first assessed across patient-derived GBM cell lines with diverse genomic drivers. The drugs pharmacokinetics (PK) and biodistribution were measured using mass spectrometry in mice bearing patient-derived orthotopic xenograft (PDX) GBM. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in two genetically distinct PDX models of recurrent GBM, administering VT104 as monotherapy or in combination with standard-of-care radiotherapy plus temozolomide (RT+TMZ). Results: VT104/VT103 treatment significantly impaired GBM proliferation and migration in-vitro, with concomitant downregulation of TEAD-target expression. PK studies confirmed sustained VT104 plasma levels and robust brain biodistribution in PDX mice, with brain:plasma ratio >150% at therapeutic dosing without systemic toxicity. While VT104 monotherapy showed modest anti-tumor effects, combination therapy (VT104+RT+TMZ) significantly extended overall survival in both recurrent GBM PDX models. The survival benefit was most prominent in EGFR-mutant GBM and corresponded to significant decrease in overall and infiltrative tumor burden. Mechanistically, VT104 potentiated TMZ-dependent {gamma}-H2AX genotoxic stress and RT+TMZ synergized with VT104 to abolish TEAD activity. Conclusion: Integrating YAP-TEAD inhibition with standard therapy introduces a clinically-relevant paradigm for synergistic treatment in recurrent GBM that both inhibits tumor infiltration and reduces therapeutic resistance to chemoradiation.

papers.title: Extra-sheath transplantation of human retinal organoids (hROs): effects on visual recovery and retinal repair following optic nerve injury
papers.abstract: Traumatic optic nerve injury interrupts retinal ganglion cell output and can produce permanent visual disability, yet a therapeutic strategy that couples retinal protection with recovery of visual-pathway activity remains unavailable. Here, we evaluated human retinal organoid transplantation at the site of optic nerve crush in C57 mice. Human retinal organoids derived from embryonic stem cells were used at day 30 and showed retinal-lineage immunoreactivity together with spontaneous microelectrode-array activity. Across post-surgical days 7, 14, and 28, transplantation was associated with preservation of optic-disc appearance and ganglion cell layer thickness. The structural benefit became statistically distinguishable from the crush group at day 28 and remained incomplete relative to the uninjured or sham group. Serial RBPMS and TUJ1 immunostaining further supported attenuation of retinal ganglion cell body and neurite loss, while IBA1 staining indicated an altered microglial response. Full-field electroretinographic b-wave responses showed no detectable between-group differences, arguing against a major outer-retinal effect. In contrast, flash visual evoked potential P2 amplitude was higher in transplanted than in crush-only mice at all measured time points, consistent with improved visual-pathway responsiveness. Transplant recipients also showed enhanced optomotor responses across tested spatial-frequency and contrast conditions. Light-dark behavior shifted toward greater dark-compartment occupancy and activity, although this assay remains non-specific for visual recovery. Together, these findings support a model in which hROs transplantation at an optic nerve injury site promotes multi-level functional preservation after optic nerve crush. Definitive evidence for donor-derived circuit reconstruction will require graft tracing, synaptic validation, and prespecified electrophysiologic analyses.

papers.title: 2-hydroxyglutarate-dependent inhibition of TET2 is a molecular link between metabolic reprogramming and smooth muscle cell differentiation
papers.abstract: Background: Smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic modulation is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but the mechanisms linking metabolism to contractile gene expression remain unclear. We investigated whether 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG), an inhibitor of ?-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, links metabolic changes to regulation of ten-eleven translocation 2 (TET2) in Acta2R179C/+ SMCs Methods: Primary wild-type (WT) and Acta2R179C/+ mouse aortic SMCs were treated with nicotinamide riboside (NR), exogenous R&L-2-HG, or cholesterol. Endogenous accumulation of L-2HG was achieved by lentivuris-mediated knockdown (KD) of L2hgdh. We assessed contractile marker expression, cellular metabolism, TET2 chromatin occupancy, and DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation. L-2HG levels were assessed using liquid chromatography/mass spectroscopy. Carotid artery 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) staining was assessed in mice after left carotid artery ligation. Results: Acta2R179C/+ SMCs have elevated 2-HG, reduced TET2 expression and chromatin occupancy, and lower 5hmC enrichment at CArG-containing SMC loci, consistent with repressed TET2 activity. NR boosts oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), reduces 2-HG in WT and mutant SMCs, increases TET2 expression and 5hmC enrichment, and reduces global 5-methylcytosine. Carotid artery 5hmC staining shows changes in the same direction, but group differences are not statistically significant. Exogenous L-2-HG attenuates NR-induced contractile marker expression in Acta2R179C/+ SMCs and also decreases contractile marker expression, reduces TET2 occupancy and 5hmC enrichment, and shifts WT SMC metabolism toward glycolysis, phenocopying the metabolic state of Acta2R179C/+ SMCs. Endogenous accumulation of L-2HG by L2hgdh KD reduces contractile markers in WT SMCS. Cholesterol reduces TET2 and contractile marker expression, decreases 5hmC enrichment, and increases global DNA methylation. Conclusions: These findings support a role for 2-HG in coupling metabolic state to epigenetic changes associated with SMC phenotypic modulation. NR-associated differentiation coincides with increased TET2 expression and DNA hydroxymethylation, identifying metabolic regulation of the SMC epigenome as a potential approach to preserving contractile gene expression.
